#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

# The Slurm script requested 4 cores for what appears to be a single-process, multi-threaded application.
# This is translated to 1 task with 4 CPUs.
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 4

# The original script specified the 'mhigh' partition.
#flux: -q mhigh

# Output file with translated placeholders. Slurm's %u (user) has no equivalent.
# Stderr will be merged with stdout by default.
#flux: -o logs/{job.name}_{job.id}.out

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU and will NOT be allocated 4GB of memory.
# #SBATCH --gres gpu:1
# #SBATCH --mem 4096

# Ensure the output directory exists before the job starts logging.
mkdir -p logs

# The python command is run directly, as this is a single-task job.
# The allocated resources (4 CPUs) are available to this process.
python task_b.py \
    --loss "triplet"  \
    --miner "BatchHard" \
	--output_path "outputs_task_c/" \
    --dataset "mit_split" \
    --dataset_config_path "./configs/mit_split.yaml" \
    --dataset_path "/home/mcv/datasets/MIT_split/" \
	--model resnet_18 \
    --embedding_size 256 \
	--batch_size 64 \
    --epochs 20

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, two essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a GPU (`--gres gpu:1`) and the request for 4GB of memory (`--mem 4096`). While the translated script is syntactically valid, it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU and will receive a default, likely insufficient, memory allocation. Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.
The script uses a hardcoded path for the dataset (`/home/mcv/datasets/MIT_split/`), which makes it non-portable and likely to fail for other users.
